status: conditional causal bus-replay estimate; not native-controller or hardware validation

policy.before: PIM-first among released requests; committed GPU returns immutable; a new GPU request cannot prolong a pending PIM command wait
policy.after: Private rank commands excluded from external CA; complete input/output epochs own the external port exclusively, draining committed returns at ownership handoff; no GPU/PIM burst interleaving inside those epochs
policy.kernel: Ordered, launched when PIM is active without looking ahead at its end; may cross the PIM boundary; AE GPU waits until completion
policy.refresh: Known per-rank refresh calendar and periodic continuation; target-rank blackout and CA pulse checked
policy.PIM_retiming: Preserve native causal gaps, shift remaining command program after a blocked command
policy.reference: Every solo GPU plan is normalized and replayed with the same causal arbiter; identical completion and zero added memory stall are required
policy.AE_GPU: Natural-cache profiled kernel durations; existing dedicated handoff microbenchmarks retained at logical-operation cold-input boundaries

limitations: The native controller has not been extended; this is an independent online bus model.
Native inter-command timing gaps are a conservative causal replay abstraction, not regenerated bank/row state.
Uniform channel/BG distribution, GPU row-hit rank0 mapping and synchronous L2-write proxy remain assumptions.
Request completion checkpoints are a GPU-progress abstraction, not a warp/SM simulator.
Natural-cache AE timings are eager, profiled, and include small timestamp overlaps; sequential replay is not a measured concurrent runtime.
No CPU dispatch latency, handoff signaling latency, or hardware queue capacity was invented; these omitted implementation costs prevent an implementation-ready latency claim.
